The second pathway involves Crassostreaxanthin B targeting induced myeloid leukemia cell differentiation protein Mcl-1, which is subsequently targeted by 1-hexene, another compound that also affects Protein kinase C eta. These two distinct pathways suggest that Crassostreaxanthin B may exert its effects through different molecular mechanisms, both of which converge on the activation of Protein kinase C eta. The integration of these pathways highlights the potential for Crassostreaxanthin B to modulate cellular processes through multiple targets, with the shared outcome of activating Protein kinase C eta. The evidence supports a mechanism where Crassostreaxanthin B influences cellular signaling through different receptors or proteins, ultimately leading to the activation of Protein kinase C eta.
